definitions.explanation: Describes a situation or feeling that is extremely difficult to bear or tolerate. A literary, elevated expression.

examples.japanese: {忍|しの}び{難|がた}い{苦|くる}しみ。
この{屈辱|くつじょく}は{忍|しの}び{難|がた}いものがある。
examples.english: This humiliation is something truly hard to bear.

examples.japanese: {忍|しの}び{難|がた}きを{忍|しの}び、{耐|た}え{難|がた}きを{耐|た}え。
examples.english: Enduring the unendurable, bearing the unbearable.
examples.notes: Famous phrase from Emperor Hirohito's 1945 radio address announcing Japan's surrender.

notes:
A literary compound adjective from {忍|しの}ぶ (to endure) + {難|がた}い (difficult to). The pattern verb stem + {難|がた}い is productive in formal Japanese.

FAMOUS USAGE:
The phrase {忍|しの}び{難|がた}きを{忍|しの}び ({耐|た}え{難|がた}きを{耐|た}え) is one of the most famous lines in modern Japanese history, from Emperor Showa's radio broadcast on August 15, 1945, announcing Japan's acceptance of the Potsdam Declaration.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {耐|た}え{難|がた}い: unbearable — near-synonym; focuses on endurance rather than patience
- {我慢|がまん}できない: can't stand it — everyday equivalent; conversational
- {堪|た}えられない: unbearable — slightly more formal than {我慢|がまん}できない
